top_choice_rationale: P001 awards the optical lattice clock to Katori and Ye: a distinct invention (magic-wavelength trapping of many neutral atoms, separate from the 2005 comb and 2012 single-ion control) realised at 10^-18 uncertainty and reproduced by independent laboratories, with a bounded two-name allocation and a citation anchored on the invention and demonstrated performance rather than on a pending redefinition of the second. The overlap with earlier prizes is a judgement but not enough to prefer no award.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile for Katori or Ye; Goran Johansson is a Chalmers colleague, weighed on the merits.
